title: What the US Movement Against Data Centers Can Learn From Abroad
gist: Interview with Paris Marx on his book Hyperscale: Ireland's grid moratorium and its pivot to dedicated private gas plants foreshadowed the US data-center backlash, and Marx argues an AI-bubble bust would leave stranded gas plants and obsolete chips.

insights.claim: Dublin's data-center moratorium (passed in 2021) was triggered by the grid operator itself saying it lacked capacity to connect more data centers.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Grid capacity, not politics, can be the binding constraint on data-center siting; watch grid-operator statements as a leading indicator.
insights.quote: It was actually the grid operator that said, “Hey, there are too many data centers.

insights.claim: Blocked from Irish grid connections, data-center operators moved to tap the gas network, then to build dedicated gas power plants, and lobbied for legislation letting private companies build electricity cables on a publicly owned grid.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: The same grid-bypass playbook (behind-the-meter gas) is now being repeated in the US; gas-turbine and pipeline demand follow.

insights.claim: Irish regulators issued emission licences letting data-center operators burn fossil fuels while warning that climate targets would become harder to meet.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Permitting-versus-climate-target conflicts are a recurring regulatory risk for fossil-powered AI campuses.

insights.claim: The US is now seeing companies race to build massive private gas power plants for data centers, a pattern Marx says he had already seen play out abroad, though US scale and speed are staggering.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Expect continued behind-the-meter gas build-out and the local opposition that comes with it.
insights.locator: The gas stuff looks so prescient

insights.claim: Google tried to keep its water use secret in The Dalles, Oregon, getting the city council to withhold figures for about a year until the community learned the data center used 29 percent of local water.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Resource-disclosure fights are a trigger for community opposition and for disclosure rules that raise project risk.
insights.locator: When did you decide to write a book

insights.claim: Netherlands and Singapore had data-center moratoriums going back to 2019, and Ireland's grid strain became evident in 2022, before ChatGPT's launch drove the generative-AI build-out.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Constraints on data-center growth predate generative AI; AI is amplifying an existing bottleneck.
insights.locator: When did you decide to write a book

insights.claim: Data centers are one of the issues that could decide key US midterm races taking place less than two weeks after publication.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Data-center siting is now an electoral issue; watch state and local policy shifts after the election.

insights.claim: Marx believes the sector is in an AI bubble and questions whether planned data centers and gas plants will even be built before demand for AI is reassessed, given constraints on turbines, chips, and other components.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Supply bottlenecks on turbines and chips could cap or delay the build-out and expose capex plans to demand reassessment.
insights.quote: I think we're in an AI bubble.
insights.locator: What happens to the physical infrastructure

insights.claim: After the dotcom bust many data-center companies went under and survivors such as Equinix bought up capacity to be ready when demand returned.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Historical precedent: distressed data-center capacity was absorbed by well-capitalized operators.
insights.locator: We often talk about the excess build-out of fiber

insights.claim: If AI chips must be cycled out within a few years, an AI-oriented data center may hold little value by the time demand returns, unlike the dotcom-era buildings.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Short hardware life undermines the idea that idle AI capacity can simply wait for demand to return; weigh depreciation risk.
insights.locator: But the issue we have now

insights.claim: If data centers fail to materialize, the associated gas plants will still exist and will seek new customers to justify their existence.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: A bust could leave fossil generation looking for demand, a second-order effect on power markets and emissions.
insights.quote: Inevitably, even if the data centers don't come, then those gas plants will exist.
insights.locator: What happens to the physical infrastructure

insights.claim: Marx wants governments to impose firmer regulation on data-center development, paired with regulation of the AI products themselves, arguing governments still buy the narrative Sam Altman sold in early 2023.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Regulatory tightening on siting and AI products is the direction of travel being advocated; monitor it as a risk to build-out plans.
insights.locator: I would like to see governments

insights.claim: Marx argues that if the resources committed to generative AI were honestly assessed, they could not be justified financially, socially, or environmentally.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: A strongly bearish, against-consensus view on AI ROI; useful as the case a skeptic would make.
insights.quote: there's no way to justify what we are doing right now
insights.locator: We should be asking, how much computation

insights.claim: The book ends with a New Zealand community-led effort to build a Māori speech-recognition model hosted on local cloud providers, presented as a non-extractive alternative to big-tech AI.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Illustrates a niche, locally governed AI model; small but a template for sovereignty-focused alternatives.
insights.locator: You ended the book with a specific example

insights.claim: Wired's Joel Khalil expects data centers could become a political flash point in Europe as countries go to the polls next year, as EU AI ambitions collide with national climate goals.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: European build-out faces collisions between national policy, local priorities, growth ambitions and climate objectives.
insights.quote: It’s hard to see how Europe could possibly have it all.

insights.claim: Google apologized for clearing more than 800 acres of forest in Finland without the necessary environmental permits for part of a data center project, and faces backlash that could bleed into elections next spring.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Permit lapses create reputational and political risk for hyperscaler expansion in Europe.

insights.claim: Texas's data-center build-out threatens years of progress on cutting air pollution, per the Texas Tribune.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Air-quality impacts of on-site generation are an emerging regulatory angle in the US.
